correctness.rationale: Any induced perfect matching forces equal selected bipartition counts; t=1 is either a nonedge or leaves a matched vertex undominated. With t>=2, all omitted vertices have selected neighbors. Each selected A vertex has at least t-1 B neighbors, while every two-or-more selected A vertices collectively see all selected B, proving Hall for any subset and hence perfect matching. Counting two independent t-subsets and Vandermonde gives coefficients and total; every larger set contains a four-vertex paired dominating subset.

Complete multipartite paired-polynomial results do not directly include a crown after deleting its matching. The abstract-only 2016 polynomial proceeding creates an acknowledged unresolved priority risk, not an automatic scientific failure.
